questions.stem: Which AWS Support plan is included for every AWS customer at no additional cost?

options.rationale: AWS Business Support+ is a paid plan that adds 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers for technical cases.
AWS Enterprise Support is a paid plan that adds a designated Technical Account Manager.
AWS Unified Operations is the highest-level paid plan, with a designated team for critical workloads.
Basic Support is included for every customer and covers account and billing questions, documentation and core Trusted Advisor checks.

questions.explanation: 'No additional cost' points to Basic Support. Technical support cases with Cloud Support Engineers start at AWS Business Support+.

questions.stem: A company on AWS Business Support+ wants a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) for proactive guidance. What is the lowest-cost way to get one?

options.text: Keep AWS Business Support+ and ask for a TAM
options.rationale: AWS Business Support+ gives 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers but does not include a TAM.

options.text: Hire AWS Professional Services for a TAM
options.rationale: Professional Services delivers project engagements; a designated TAM comes with a support plan.
AWS Unified Operations includes a TAM, but it is a higher-priced plan than Enterprise Support.
AWS Enterprise Support is the lowest-priced plan that includes a designated TAM.

questions.explanation: AWS Business Support+ adds 24/7 technical help and the full set of Trusted Advisor checks, but no TAM. AWS Enterprise Support is the first plan with a designated TAM; AWS Unified Operations also has one at a higher price.

questions.stem: A small company needs 24/7 phone, web and chat access to AWS Cloud Support Engineers, with fast help when a business-critical system is down. It does not need a TAM. Which is the lowest-cost AWS Support plan that meets these needs?

options.rationale: Basic Support covers account and billing questions but not technical support cases.
AWS Enterprise Support meets the needs but adds a designated TAM at a higher price.
AWS Business Support+ gives 24/7 phone, web and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers and a response within 30 minutes for business-critical system down cases.
AWS Unified Operations is the highest-priced plan, with a designated team for mission-critical workloads.

questions.explanation: Around-the-clock technical help without a TAM points to AWS Business Support+. Enterprise Support is the nearest choice, but its extras, a designated TAM and a faster production-critical response, aren't needed here.

questions.stem: Which service recommends ways to reduce cost, improve performance and close security gaps, based on AWS best practices?

options.rationale: The Health Dashboard reports AWS service events.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
Trusted Advisor inspects your account and makes best-practice recommendations.
Marketplace is a software catalog.

questions.explanation: The clue is best-practice recommendations for your own account; the Health Dashboard reports AWS events instead. Basic Support includes the core checks, and AWS Business Support+ and higher plans include the full set.

questions.stem: Where can a customer see AWS events that might affect its own resources, such as scheduled maintenance or a service issue in its Region?

options.rationale: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
CloudTrail records API calls made in your account.
CloudWatch dashboards show metrics and alarms from your own resources, not AWS maintenance or service events.
The Health Dashboard shows service events, planned changes and notifications that affect your AWS resources.

questions.explanation: The clue is AWS events, such as maintenance or a service issue, that affect your resources. The AWS Health API gives programmatic access to the same events.

questions.stem: Which community-driven question-and-answer service lets customers ask technical questions about AWS and get answers from the community, including AWS experts?

options.rationale: re:Post is a community question-and-answer service for AWS.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
Marketplace is a software catalog.
The Health Dashboard reports service events.

questions.explanation: The AWS Knowledge Center is part of re:Post.

questions.stem: A company sees that an AWS resource it does not own is sending spam to its users. Whom should it report this to?

options.rationale: Professional Services helps customers deliver projects on AWS.

options.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team
options.rationale: Trust and Safety handles reports of abuse involving AWS resources.

options.text: An AWS Partner Network consulting partner
options.rationale: APN consulting partners help customers build on AWS; they do not handle abuse reports.
The Health Dashboard shows AWS events that affect your account, not abuse reports.

questions.explanation: Abuse of AWS resources, such as email spam or malware distribution, is reported to the AWS Trust and Safety team. AWS Support and the documentation feedback forms do not handle abuse reports.

questions.stem: Which AWS team of experts helps customers achieve specific business outcomes on AWS, often working alongside AWS Partners?

options.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team
options.rationale: Trust and Safety handles abuse reports.
re:Post is a community Q&A service.
AWS Professional Services is a global team of experts that helps customers achieve specific outcomes on AWS.
Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.explanation: Other sources of expert help include AWS Solutions Architects and partners in the AWS Partner Network.

questions.stem: A company wants help from a third-party consulting firm that specializes in AWS migrations. Where should it look?

options.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team
options.rationale: Trust and Safety handles reports of abuse involving AWS resources.
The Health Dashboard reports AWS events that affect your account.
Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.
The AWS Partner Network (APN) includes consulting partners and system integrators with AWS expertise.

questions.explanation: The clue is a third-party firm, which points to the AWS Partner Network. APN also includes independent software vendors (ISVs) that sell through AWS Marketplace.

questions.stem: Which resource provides time-tested strategies, guides and patterns from AWS and AWS Partners for migration and modernization projects?

options.rationale: Trusted Advisor checks your own account against best practices; it does not publish migration guides.
Prescriptive Guidance offers strategies, guides and patterns for common projects such as migration.
The Health Dashboard reports AWS events that affect your account.
Marketplace is a catalog for finding and buying third-party software.

questions.explanation: Technical resources include AWS documentation, whitepapers, blogs, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re:Post.

questions.stem: Which TWO are categories of AWS Trusted Advisor checks? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Data sovereignty is not a Trusted Advisor category.
Machine learning is not a Trusted Advisor category.
Trusted Advisor checks for issues such as open ports and root MFA.
Licensing is not a Trusted Advisor category.
Trusted Advisor finds idle and underused resources.

questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor categories include cost optimization, performance, resilience (fault tolerance), security, operational excellence and service limits.

questions.stem: A company runs mission-critical workloads and wants a designated TAM plus domain specialist engineers, with a response within 5 minutes during critical incidents. Which should it choose?

options.rationale: AWS Enterprise Support has a designated TAM and up to 15-minute production-critical response, but not domain specialist engineers.
Professional Services is a consulting team for projects, not a support plan.
AWS Unified Operations adds a designated TAM and domain specialist engineers, with incident engineers who respond within 5 minutes.
AWS Business Support+ gives 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers but no designated TAM.

questions.explanation: Domain specialist engineers and a 5-minute critical response point to AWS Unified Operations. Enterprise Support is the nearest plan: it also has a designated TAM, but not that dedicated team.

questions.stem: A company wants to find, buy and deploy security software from independent software vendors (ISVs), with the charges on its AWS bill. Which should it use?

options.rationale: Service Catalog lets an organization publish its own curated catalog of approved AWS resources.
AWS Marketplace is a catalog where customers find, buy, deploy and manage software from ISVs and other sellers.
The AWS Partner Network is the program that partner companies such as ISVs join; it is not where customers buy software.
License Manager manages software licenses you already have.

questions.explanation: The clue is buying third-party software and paying through the AWS bill, which is AWS Marketplace. The AWS Partner Network is the program those ISVs belong to, not the store.

questions.stem: A company wants its own operations tool to pull information about AWS events that affect its account, such as scheduled maintenance, by calling an API. What should it use?

options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls made in your account, not AWS service events.
Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices.
The AWS Health API gives programmatic access to the events shown in the AWS Health Dashboard; it needs AWS Business Support+ or a higher plan.
CloudWatch collects metrics and logs from your own resources.

questions.explanation: 'Calling an API' for AWS events points to the AWS Health API; the Health Dashboard shows the same events in the console. CloudTrail is the nearest trap, but it logs actions taken in your account.
